name: Ghostonix Mail SMTP
author: ghostonix

sections.description:
Ghostonix Mail SMTP helps WordPress and WooCommerce site owners replace the default WordPress sender identity with a professional sender such as noreply@yourdomain.com, orders@yourdomain.com, or support@yourdomain.com.

The plugin can force the From Name, From Email, and Reply-To headers for outgoing site emails. SMTP delivery is optional. If SMTP is enabled, the plugin routes mail through the SMTP server configured by the site owner.

Core features:

  • Force From Name and From Email.
  • Optional Reply-To Name and Reply-To Email.
  • Optional SMTP host, port, encryption, username, and password.
  • Test email tool.
  • Local sent/failed email logs.
  • WooCommerce-compatible sender control.
  • Password storage with encryption when OpenSSL is available.

This plugin does not provide a hosted email delivery service. It does not generate DNS records, CNAME records, DKIM records, SPF records, or DMARC records. DNS authentication is handled by the email provider or domain/email host used by the site owner.

If SMTP is enabled, your WordPress site connects directly to the SMTP server you configure, such as your email host or transactional email provider. Ghostonix Mail SMTP does not send email content, SMTP settings, SMTP credentials, or local mail logs to Ghostonix servers.

Ghostonix Mail SMTP includes optional upgrade/account functionality powered by the Freemius SDK. Freemius may be used for license activation, paid upgrades, software updates, account management, and opt-in telemetry. Freemius is contacted only when a site owner chooses an account, license, update, opt-in, or upgrade action. When a site owner chooses to opt in, activate a license, or purchase/upgrade, selected site, admin, plugin, license, and payment-related data may be sent to Freemius according to Freemius policies.

Freemius Terms of Service: https://freemius.com/terms/
Freemius Privacy Policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/

Privacy

Ghostonix Mail SMTP stores plugin settings and local email logs in your WordPress database. Logs may include recipient email addresses, email subjects, sender details, timestamps, and delivery status. The plugin does not transmit email content, SMTP settings, SMTP credentials, or local mail logs to Ghostonix servers.

If you enable SMTP, your site will connect to the SMTP server you configure. The privacy and terms of that SMTP provider apply to email sent through that provider.

Optional upgrade, license, account, update, and opt-in telemetry functionality is powered by Freemius. Freemius is contacted only when a site owner chooses an account, license, update, opt-in, or upgrade action. Freemius may collect selected site, admin, plugin, license, and payment-related data when a site owner opts in, activates a license, or purchases/upgrades. See the Freemius Terms of Service and Privacy Policy linked above.

Usage Notice

All Ghostonix plugins are built to help WordPress/WooCommerce site owners save time, reduce technical friction, and avoid unnecessary custom development. Before installing, updating, or activating any Ghostonix plugin on a live website, users are responsible for testing it on a staging or development environment.

Because WordPress sites can vary based on themes, plugins, hosting environments, custom code, outdated software, and third-party configurations, Ghostonix does not guarantee conflict-free operation on every website. Ghostonix is not responsible for issues caused by broken code, misconfigured websites, unsupported third-party plugins/themes, server limitations, or conflicts outside Ghostonix’s control.

By installing, activating, or using any Ghostonix plugin, the user agrees to Ghostonix’s Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, Refund Policy, and any other applicable policies published on our official website.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install it through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open Ghostonix Mail SMTP in the WordPress admin sidebar.
  4. Enter your From Name and From Email.
  5. Save settings.
  6. Send a test email.
  7. Optional: enable SMTP and enter your SMTP credentials.
sections.faq:
Can this replace the default WordPress sender with noreply@yourdomain.com?

Yes. Enable sender control, set the From Name and From Email, save settings, and send a test email.

Is SMTP required?

No. The plugin can control the sender identity without SMTP. SMTP is recommended when you want authenticated delivery through your own email provider.

Does this plugin create CNAME, DKIM, SPF, or DMARC records?

No. Those records are created by your email provider or domain/email host. This plugin only controls WordPress sender settings and optionally connects WordPress to the SMTP server you configure.

Does this plugin send email data to Ghostonix?

No. Ghostonix Mail SMTP does not send email content, SMTP settings, SMTP credentials, or local mail logs to Ghostonix servers.

Where are logs stored?

Logs are stored locally in the WordPress database on the site where the plugin is installed.

Is WooCommerce supported?

Yes. WooCommerce emails use WordPress mail, so this plugin can control the WooCommerce sender identity.
